tools.name: preflight
tools.description: Returns one signed go/no-go decision (allow, warn, require_confirmation, block or unsupported) for one action on one domain: read, cite, connect, transact or administer. Use it before acting on a site you have not checked. Pass agent (your crawler token) to have robots.txt checked. For the evidence

tools.name: best_source
tools.description: Ranks 2 to 10 candidate sites, or the measured businesses for a trade and city, by what CrawlCheck verified, with signed reasons for and against each. Sites that share a phone number or homepage text are grouped as one network. Use when choosing which business or site to cite, recommend or call. For

tools.name: resolve_domain
tools.description: Returns the full signed record for one domain: what it claims, what each crawler is actually served, who controls it, a decision per action, what changed, and the evidence and time behind each part. A domain never measured gets a partial answer naming what was not read. For one go/no-go decision use

tools.name: field_check
tools.description: Returns a signed verdict on one business fact you hold (phone, address, hours or service area), checked against the business's own site and its dated history. Verdicts include matches, former_value, not_this_business and not_published. Use before repeating or acting on a business's contact details.

tools.name: scan_domain
tools.description: Scans a domain now (5-15 seconds) and returns its graded record: grade, score, section scores and findings. CrawlCheck's scanner sends other crawlers' user-agent strings, so site logs show those names; they are not visits by those crawlers. A domain scanned in the last 2 minutes returns that report,

tools.name: list_verified_capabilities
tools.description: Lists what a domain declares agents can do (OpenAPI operations, MCP tools, A2A skills, API catalog entries), each classed by safety, which ones CrawlCheck called and confirmed, and every mismatch. Read from the latest scan on file; run scan_domain first mcp_servers

Which remote MCP servers the official MCP Registry lists on a domain, and what each endpoint actually answered when CrawlCheck sent the MCP handshake (initialized, auth_required, unreachable, tool count, tool-list drift). Use before selecting an MCP tool from that domain.

tools.name: verify_crawler_log
tools.description: Given raw web-server access-log lines, decide for each line that names a crawler (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Googlebot, PerplexityBot...) whether the source IP falls inside that operator's published ranges. Returns verified, spoofed, or unverifiable when the operator publishes no ranges.

tools.name: corpus_state
tools.description: Use to judge how representative CrawlCheck's public dataset is before quoting its figures. Returns how many distinct domains have been measured, how they split by platform, rendering, size, language and kind, and which strata are still under-sampled. No input; read-only. For CrawlCheck's headline fi

tools.name: resolve_robots
tools.description: Resolve every named answer engine, search index and training crawler against a domain's robots.txt the way a crawler does: most-specific group only, longest match, allow wins a tie. Shows when a Disallow under * does not apply to an agent with its own group.

tools.name: resolve_rights
tools.description: What a site declares AI may do with a page, one answer per use (train, ground, summarize, cite, transact), merged from robots.txt read per agent, Content-Signal, ai.txt, TDM-Rep, robots meta, X-Robots-Tag and the terms page, with the signal that decided each answer and every conflict between signals

tools.name: check_site_safety
tools.description: Use when the only question is whether a site is listed as dangerous, before an agent reads, cites, links to or pays it. Returns whether it is listed as malware or phishing (Google Safe Browsing, a public malware-blocking DNS resolver, PhishTank), which list says so, where to check it and where its o

tools.name: draft_llms
tools.description: Draft an llms.txt from the domain's own homepage and up to 25 declared pages, using their titles and descriptions. A draft for the owner to cut down, not a publication.

tools.name: fix_robots
tools.description: The domain's served robots.txt, corrected: * group rules copied into named groups that lacked them (shadowing), a Sitemap line added when missing, a minimal replacement when the served file was HTML. Every change is listed at the top; nothing else is touched.

tools.name: fix_entitymap
tools.description: Use when a site has no entitymap.json, or to replace a wrong one. Returns a starter entitymap.json built from the domain's latest scan record: business name, phone, coordinates and declared service areas as entities with SERVES relations. Fields the site never stated are marked TODO, never guessed.

tools.name: video_check
tools.description: Use to audit one YouTube video for search and AI visibility. Returns twelve checks against the video anchor model (metadata, chapters, captions and storyboard where observed), each naming what it read and whether it passed. Read-only; results are cached for six hours unless fresh is true. For a chan

tools.name: video_channel
tools.description: Use to list a YouTube channel's uploads. Returns every upload on the channel, read 50 at a time and sorted by views. Give handle or, without one, the channel id. The per-check tally needs a Watch licence and is not offered here. Read-only. For the checks on one video use video_check.

tools.name: video_site
tools.description: Use to check how a website carries its videos. Reads the homepage plus up to 60 sitemap pages for YouTube embeds, facades and page-builder widgets, VideoObject nodes and their required properties, and, given a channel handle, how many of the channel's videos the site carries. Read-only. For one vide

tools.name: registry_lookup
tools.description: Whether a domain is in CrawlCheck's registry and what it serves: llms.txt, agents.md, a media kit at /.well-known/media-kit.json, a reciprocity-tested entity graph, an AI access policy that names crawlers, and agent-callable surfaces. With no domain, returns the shelf counts across every measured si

tools.name: crawler_path
tools.description: Where each crawler's path into a domain dies, as an observed data flow: edge decision, robots.txt as a file, robots.txt rules, then the page, JSON-LD, sitemap, llms.txt and entitymap.json it reached. Give agent (e.g. ClaudeBot, GPTBot, googlebot) for one identity's path and a one-line answer; omit i

tools.name: public_counts
tools.description: Use when you need to quote one of CrawlCheck's figures about itself. Returns them read from the source: sites_measured, domains_in_corpus, crawler_visits (a rolling window), sections, sections_scored, findings_published, guides_published, with an at timestamp. No input; read-only. For dataset covera

tools.name: telemetry
tools.description: Verified-crawler traffic observed at crawlcheck.io itself: which named agents arrived, how many claims were confirmed against operator ranges, how many were forged.

tools.name: fix_mostly_code
tools.description: A fix plan for PAGE_IS_MOSTLY_CODE: the homepage's measured bytes by category, the largest blocks with what to do with each, ordered steps with the text ratio after each, and the step at which the detector would stop firing - or, when moving code cannot clear it, how much markup to cut or text to ad

tools.name: fix_stale_cache
tools.description: Use after a scan reports STALE_CACHE_SERVED (visitors and crawlers get an old cached homepage). tools.name: fix_machine_chain
tools.description: Use after a scan reports MACHINE_CHAIN_HEAVY (crawlers must read too many or too large files before the page). Returns a fix plan: the files a crawler reads before the page and the 404s that absent agent files return, then measured reductions (llms.txt to an index, a sitemap index, robots.txt commen

tools.name: explain_finding
tools.description: Why CrawlCheck decided a finding: the rule and its revision, the exact fetches it compared (identity, status, bytes, sha256), when the condition held on the site, and a Merkle proof that the decision is inside the signed manifest. Give id (a d1: decision or f1: finding id from a report), or domain a

tools.name: machine_record
tools.description: The unified machine record for one observation: subject, grade, findings (in full), capabilities with verification, and the evidence roots, manifest and verifier links that let anyone check it offline. Give id (report, d1:, f1: or manifest sha256) or domain for the latest.

tools.name: mcp_precheck
tools.description: For MCP server publishers, before releasing a new version. Give the server name (as listed in the MCP Registry) or its endpoint, the new tools/list result and the new serverInfo.version; with no tools the endpoint is read as it serves now. Returns, against CrawlCheck's last read of that server, what

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "field_check" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Call before using a phone number, address, opening hours or service area you hold for a business. One signed verdict per business field. field=phone|address|hou…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "explain_finding" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: id, domain, code, path

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_site_safety, fix_stale_cache, fix_machine_chain · Private data: preflight, resolve_domain, scan_domain, list_verified_capabilities, check_site_safety, fix_robots, fix_entitymap, crawler_path, fix_machine_chain, machine_record, mcp_precheck · Public sink: best_source, video_check, video_channel, explain_finding · Destructive: fix_entitymap.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_site_safety, fix_stale_cache, fix_machine_chain · Private data: preflight, resolve_domain, scan_domain, list_verified_capabilities, check_site_safety, fix_robots, fix_entitymap, crawler_path, fix_machine_chain, machine_record, mcp_precheck · Public sink: best_source, video_check, video_channel, explain_finding · Destructive: fix_entitymap

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
